name: Rizatriptan
summary: An orally fast-acting triptan with roughly three times the oral bioavailability of sumatriptan, widely used for acute migraine attacks.
mechanism: Selective 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonist — constricts dilated cranial vessels and inhibits trigeminal nociceptive signaling.

dosing.adult: 10 mg PO at onset (5 mg if taking propranolol); may repeat after 2 h

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; no clear major teratogenicity — use the lowest effective frequency
contraindications: Ischemic heart disease or coronary vasospasm (including Prinzmetal angina)
Ergotamines or other triptans within 24 h
warnings: Coronary vasospasm/ischemia — assess cardiovascular risk before first use
Serotonin syndrome when combined with SSRIs/SNRIs/MAOIs
Propranolol increases rizatriptan levels — halve the dose
Medication-overuse headache if used more than ~2 days/week
monitoring: Cardiovascular risk assessment before first dose
safety.overdose: Hypertension, chest symptoms; mostly benign, supportive care

indications: Acute migraine with or without aura
clinicalPearls: Fastest oral onset of the common triptans (~30 min) with higher bioavailability than sumatriptan tablets
Halve to 5 mg whenever the patient is on propranolol — levels rise substantially
good: Rapid oral migraine relief with better bioavailability than sumatriptan tablets.
bad: Same cardiovascular exclusions as all triptans; needs dose reduction with propranolol.
